new.title: Admire the twin minarets of the Çifte Minareli Medrese
new.desc: A Seljuk madrasa from the late 13th century, also called the Hatuniye Medrese, and the symbol of Erzurum. Its portal is flanked by two tall fluted minarets of brick and tile, and the building now serves as a museum.
new.tip: Entry is free or very cheap; late afternoon light is best on the portal. Üç Kümbetler is a few minutes' walk south.
new.q: Çifte Minareli Medrese, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Explore the Yakutiye Medresesi and its museum
new.desc: Built in 1310 by Hoca Yakut Gazani under the Ilkhanid sultan Olcayto, it is one of the largest courtyard madrasas in Anatolia. Today it houses the Turkish-Islamic Arts and Ethnography Museum.
new.tip: Look at the carved stone portal and the brick minaret with its turquoise tile bands. Next door is the Ulu Cami.
new.q: Yakutiye Medresesi, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: See the conical Üç Kümbetler tombs
new.desc: Three Seljuk-era mausoleums with cone-shaped roofs; the largest is thought to be the tomb of Emir Saltuk from the late 12th century, the others from the 14th century.
new.tip: Free to walk around, and the tombs sit just south of the Çifte Minareli Medrese. The Erzurum Museum is beside them.
new.q: Üç Kümbetler, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Climb Erzurum Castle and its clock tower
new.desc: The Byzantine-founded citadel (the İçkale) overlooks the old city, with a Seljuk mescit and a later Ottoman clock tower inside the walls. Views stretch over the rooftops and the Palandöken range.
new.tip: Go late afternoon for the light over the city. The Kurşunlu Mosque stands on the nearby slope.
new.q: Erzurum Kalesi, Kale Mahallesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Step inside the Erzurum Ulu Cami
new.desc: Built in 1179 by the Saltuklu emir Nasreddin Aslan Mehmet and also called the Atabey Mosque, it is one of the oldest mosques in Erzurum. Its forest of stone pillars and plain Seljuk interior contrast with the ornate madrasa next door.
new.tip: Dress modestly and avoid prayer times. It is a two-minute walk from the Yakutiye.
new.q: Erzurum Ulu Cami, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Visit the Lala Mustafa Paşa Mosque
new.desc: Commissioned in 1562 by Lala Mustafa Pasha while he was governor of Erzurum and attributed to the architect Sinan. It is a compact classical Ottoman mosque with a tidy courtyard.
new.tip: Quiet outside prayer times. It is close to the Taşhan bazaar.
new.q: Lala Mustafa Paşa Camii, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Tour the Erzurum Museum beside the Üç Kümbetler
new.desc: The provincial archaeology and ethnography museum covers Urartian, Roman and Byzantine finds from the Erzurum plain and eastern Anatolia, with Ottoman-era ethnographic displays.
new.tip: Hours and tickets change; museum cards are generally accepted. Pair it with the Üç Kümbetler.
new.q: Erzurum Müzesi, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Walk through the Atatürk House Museum in Erzurum
new.desc: The mansion where Mustafa Kemal stayed during the 1919 Erzurum Congress, restored and opened as a museum in 2003. Rooms keep period furniture and personal items from the National Struggle.
new.tip: Check opening days before going; it is a short walk from the Congress Building.
new.q: Atatürk Evi Müzesi, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Pay respects at Aziziye Tabya and Nene Hatun's grave
new.desc: One of the Ottoman bastions built on the hills around Erzurum, Aziziye saw fierce fighting in the 1877-78 war with Russia. The heroine Nene Hatun, who joined the defence, is buried here.
new.tip: The hill gives wide views of the city; go by car or taxi. Free to enter.
new.q: Aziziye Tabyası, Aziziye Mahallesi, Aziziye, Erzurum

new.title: Shop for Oltu stone beads in Rüstem Paşa Bedesteni
new.desc: The two-storey caravanserai built in 1561 by Grand Vizier Rüstem Pasha now holds around a hundred workshops and shops selling prayer beads, rings and jewellery cut from Oltu stone, a local black jet.
new.tip: Ask for the real stone (warm to the touch and light); bargain politely. Çay in the courtyard is a good pause.
new.q: Rüstem Paşa Bedesteni (Taşhan), Cumhuriyet Caddesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Eat cağ kebab at Gelgör Gürcükapı
new.desc: Cağ kebab is horizontal lamb cooked on a rotating skewer over wood, served one skewer at a time with lavaş and onion. Gelgör has served it since 1982 near the Gürcükapı gate.
new.tip: Order by the skewer and say when to stop; the kadayıf dolması is a popular follow-up. Open from morning to late evening.
new.q: Gelgör Cağ Kebap Gürcükapı, Orhan Şerifsoy Caddesi, Kazım Karabekir Paşa Mahallesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Eat Erzurum su böreği at Anadolu Su Böreği
new.desc: Erzurum's registered su böreği is made from many thin layers, fried on a stove rather than baked, and filled with civil cheese or minced meat. Anadolu is known for its 13-layer version and also makes mantı.
new.tip: Try the civil peynirli version; it is mostly a breakfast and lunch place.
new.q: Anadolu Su Böreği & Mantı, Leylak Sokak, Recep Akdağ Bulvarı 18/A, Rabia Ana Mahallesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Taste kesme aşı at Tarihi Erzurum Evleri
new.desc: A restaurant built from linked old stone houses and a former inn, serving local dishes such as kesme aşı (hand-cut noodles in yoghurt sauce), lor dolması and kadayıf dolması.
new.tip: Good for a sit-down Erzurum meal; confirm opening hours and live-music evenings first.
new.q: Tarihi Erzurum Evleri, Yüzbaşı Reşit Bey Sokak, İbrahimpaşa Mahallesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Eat altı ezmeli köfte at Emirşeyh Köftecisi
new.desc: A long-established Erzurum köfte house on Tebriz Kapı Caddesi, known for its signature altı ezmeli köfte, served over a bed of crushed bread and butter. The menu also has saç kavurma and cağ kebab.
new.tip: It gets busy at lunchtime, so arrive early. Order the köfte with a side of ayran.
new.q: Emirşeyh Köftecisi, Tebriz Kapı Caddesi No:170, Rabia Ana Mahallesi, Yakutiye, Erzurum

new.title: Ski or ride the lifts at Palandöken
new.desc: Palandöken is Turkey's best-known ski resort, rising above Erzurum to about 3,100 m and part of Ejder 3200 World Ski Center. It hosted the 2011 Winter Universiade.
new.tip: Season runs roughly December to April; lift passes and gear rental are at the base. The resort is about 10 minutes from the city centre.
new.q: Palandöken Kayak Merkezi, Yunusemre, Palandöken, Erzurum

new.title: Ski the quieter slopes at Konaklı
new.desc: Konaklı is the western section of the Ejder 3200 ski area, with its own lifts and gentler, less crowded runs than Palandöken, sitting about 17-22 km from the city.
new.tip: Check which runs are open and whether artificial snow is running; a shuttle or taxi is needed from town.
new.q: Konaklı Kayak Merkezi, Konaklı, Palandöken, Erzurum

new.title: Soak in the Aziziye Ilıca thermal springs
new.desc: The Ilıca (Aziziye) thermal area lies high on the plateau near Erzurum, with sodium-bicarbonate water at roughly 39 degrees, used for joint and skin complaints.
new.tip: Best after a day on the slopes in winter; check the facility you choose is open.
new.q: Ilıca Kaplıcaları, Ilıca Mahallesi, Aziziye, Erzurum

new.title: Stand at the top of Tortum Waterfall
new.desc: The Tortum Waterfall in the Tev valley is about 48 m high and 21 m wide, one of the tallest in Türkiye. It feeds the Tortum Çayı towards Lake Tortum.
new.tip: Spring melt gives the biggest flow. Viewing platforms and picnic spots are by the road.
new.q: Tortum Şelalesi, Tortum, Erzurum

new.title: Find the frescoes of Öşvank Monastery
new.desc: A 10th-century Georgian church built between 963 and 973 in Çamlıyamaç village, Uzundere. Its large cathedral still has carved reliefs and inscriptions, though weather has worn much of the decoration.
new.tip: The road is rough in places and conditions vary by season; the site is free and unstaffed.
new.q: Öşvank Kilisesi, Çamlıyamaç Köyü, Uzundere, Erzurum

new.title: See the Haho Church (Taş Camii) in Bağbaşı
new.desc: A Georgian church of the Bagratid era built around 976-1001 and later turned into a mosque; it is also called Meryem Ana Kilisesi. It stands in Bağbaşı village near Tortum Lake.
new.tip: The interior is often closed outside prayer times because of restoration. Combine with Tortum Lake and the waterfall.
new.q: Haho Kilisesi (Taş Camii), Bağbaşı Köyü, Tortum, Erzurum

new.title: Watch the red fairy chimneys of Narman at sunset
new.desc: Sedimentary red sandstone formations in valleys south of Narman, about 90 km from Erzurum, on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list. The area runs through three valleys totalling some 62 km.
new.tip: Visit near sunset when the rock glows; the area has no entry fee.
new.q: Narman Peribacaları, Narman, Erzurum

new.title: Climb Hasankale Castle in Pasinler
new.desc: A hill fortress above Pasinler, about 40 km east of Erzurum, long fought over; a Roman victory here is recorded in the 4th century.
new.tip: Pair it with the Pasinler hot springs; wear shoes with grip for the climb.
new.q: Hasankale Kalesi, Pasinler, Erzurum

new.title: Bathe in the Pasinler hot springs
new.desc: Pasinler Kaplıcaları is one of the best-known thermal sites of Erzurum province, about 40 km east of the city, with mineral water used for rheumatism and skin complaints.
new.tip: Choose a facility with separate hours for men and women; it combines well with Hasankale Castle.
new.q: Pasinler Kaplıcası, Pasinler, Erzurum

new.title: Look over the Çoruh from İspir Castle
new.desc: A Saltuklu-era castle on a commanding hill beside the Erzurum-Artvin road, overlooking the Çoruh valley and town of İspir.
new.tip: The view over the river is the draw; it is free and best in morning light.
new.q: İspir Kalesi, İspir, Erzurum

new.title: Climb Oltu Castle above the town
new.desc: A fortress above the bus station in central Oltu, traced to the Urartians and heavily restored in 1998-99. It looks over the town in the Oltu stone region.
new.tip: Free to enter; the climb is short. Oltu is also known for its cağ kebab and Oltu stone beads.
new.q: Oltu Kalesi, Oltu, Erzurum

new.title: Walk the walls of Bayburt Castle
new.desc: A castle with about 3 km of walls, rebuilt in the early 13th century by Tuğrul Şah of Erzurum, also known as Çinimaçin for the tile decoration. Excavations have uncovered Bronze Age traces.
new.tip: Check which sections are open during restoration; the hill gives views over the Çoruh valley.
new.q: Bayburt Kalesi, Bayburt Merkez, Bayburt

new.title: Visit the Baksı Museum in Bayraktar village
new.desc: A contemporary art and ethnography museum founded by Hüsamettin Koçan, with the main building completed in 2010 on a hillside above the Çoruh valley. It lies about 45 km from Bayburt and has won international architecture awards.
new.tip: Open daily except Monday, around 10:00-19:00; confirm before the drive.
new.q: Baksı Müzesi, Bayraktar Köyü, Bayburt

new.title: Descend into the Aydıntepe Underground City
new.desc: A network of rock-cut galleries and rooms about 2-2.5 m below the streets of Aydıntepe, roughly 25 km from Bayburt. About 850 m of it is open to the public.
new.tip: Mind your head; cool inside year-round.
new.q: Aydıntepe Yeraltı Şehri, Aydıntepe, Bayburt

new.title: Visit the Dede Korkut Tomb near Masat
new.desc: A domed tomb near Yıldırım (Masat) village, about 39 km from Bayburt, traditionally linked with the Oghuz sage Dede Korkut. The International Dede Korkut Culture and Art Festival is held here each July.
new.tip: Go in July if you can, when the festival takes place.
new.q: Dede Korkut Türbesi, Yıldırım Köyü, Bayburt

new.title: See the Bayburt Ulu Cami
new.desc: A historic mosque in central Bayburt, with an inscription over the door showing repairs in 1550.
new.tip: Dress modestly; visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Bayburt Ulu Camii, Bayburt Merkez, Bayburt

new.title: Browse the Kenan Yavuz Ethnography Museum
new.desc: A private ethnography museum in Beşpınar village in the Demirözü valley, founded by businessman Kenan Yavuz and awarded by the European Museum Forum.
new.tip: The grounds host harvest festivals and Dede Korkut events in season.
new.q: Kenan Yavuz Etnografya Müzesi, Beşpınar Köyü, Demirözü, Bayburt

new.title: Eat sac tava at Baycanbaba in Bayburt
new.desc: A well-rated döner and sac tava house in central Bayburt. Bayburt tava, meat cooked on a sac, is a staple of local restaurants.
new.tip: Check hours: reviews suggest it opens around 09:00.
new.q: Baycanbaba Döner Sac Tava, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:90, Bayburt Merkez, Bayburt

new.title: Have breakfast at UvaPark in Bayburt
new.desc: A highly rated breakfast and dessert cafe in central Bayburt.
new.tip: Come mid-morning for the full spread.
new.q: UvaPark Kahvaltı & Tatlı, Sahil Yolu Caddesi No:5, Bayburt Merkez, Bayburt
